info.name: Teamtailor API
info.description:
The Teamtailor API follows the JSON API Specification.

If you have any questions or feedback, please contact us at support@teamtailor.com

Example use cases:

  • Add/Import candidates and get detailed information about candidates

  • Build a custom career site. Display info about jobs, departments and locations.

  • List current job openings, get detailed information and create new jobs

URLs for EU or NA stack:

When calling Teamtailor’s Public API, the base URL will depend on the stack where your data is being stored.

Request URLs:

  • For EU stack, use api.teamtailor.com

  • For NA stack, use api.na.teamtailor.com

Authentication

GET https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Token token=abc123abc123

Authenticate your account when using the API by including your secret API key in the request. Manage your API keys.

Authentication is performed by passing the api key in the Authorization header.

You must replace _abc123abc123_ it with your own API key.

Permissions

Your api keys might have different scopes and permissions.

Public

Has access to public data, basically all data that is publicly visible on your career site.

read

Can read all public data, for example, jobs, departments, and locations.

write

Can create new jobs.

read/write

Can do all above and update existing jobs.

Internal

Same as Public, but can also access internal, unlisted & archived jobs.

read

Can read all public & internal data, for example jobs, departments, locations.

write

Can create new jobs.

read/write

Can do all above and update existing jobs.

Admin

Has access to all resources.

read

Can read all data, for example candidates, jobs, users.

write

Can create new jobs, candidates and job applications.

read/write

Can do all above and update jobs, candidates and job applications.

Versioning

GET https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?filter[department]=337 HTTP/1.1
X-Api-Version : 20240404

When we make backwards-incompatible changes to the API, we release new, dated versions. You can use todays date as X-Api-Version to always get the latest version of the API.

To set the API version on a specific request, send a X-Api-Version header. See the API changelog to see current and old versions.

The X-Api-Version header is required when making requests to the API

Successful API requests will have the used API version in the response header X-Api-Version

Rate limits & large dataset handling

Handling Large Payloads:

Some endpoints, like /v1/answers or /v1/actions, may return massive datasets. Attempting to fetch all data in a single request can lead to HTTP 500 errors. To avoid this: use filtering, pagination or batch requests.

Rate Limits:

You get a bucket of 50 requests every 10 seconds. When the number of requests reaches the rate limit, the api will respond with HTTP status code 429.

Headers 

X-Rate-Limit-Limit
# The number of allowed requests in the current period
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining
# The number of remaining requests in the current period
X-Rate-Limit-Reset
# The number of seconds left in the current period

Pagination

Example response 

{
  "meta": {
    "record-count": 2,
    "page-count": 1
  },
  "links": {
    "prev": "https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?filter[department]=337&page[before]=NQ&page[size]=10&sort=id",
    "next": "https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?filter[department]=337&page[after]=Ng&page[size]=10&sort=id",
  }
}

All top-level API resources have support for bulk fetches via "list" API methods.

The links key in the response may contain any of the following links:

  • first: the first page of data

  • last: the last page of data

  • prev: the previous page of data

  • next: the next page of data

The meta key contains:

  • record-count: The total number of items in the collection,

  • page-count: The number of pages

The page size can be changed with the following parameter:

  • page[size], the number of resources per page. Default: 10, max: 30.

Examples

Here are some real world usage examples of the Teamtailor API.

Paginate a list

Get the first page of jobs, with 20 jobs per page.

GET <a class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml'  rel="noreferrer noopener nofollow" href="https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?page[size]=20&page[numb" target="_blank" url="https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?page[size]=20&page[numb">https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?page[size]=20</a> HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Token token=abc123abc123
X-Api-Version: 20240404

Parameters used in this example

Parameter Value Description
page[size] 20 Get 20 jobs in the list.

List published jobs with their department and locations

Get a list of published jobs and include their departments and locations in one request.

GET https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs?include=department,locations HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Token token=abc123abc123
X-Api-Version: 20240404

Parameters used in this example

Parameter Value Description

List latest hired candidates

Get a list of the most recent hired candidates

GET https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/job-applications?include=candidate&filter[stage-type]=hired&sort=-changed_stage_at HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Token token=abc123abc123
X-Api-Version: 20240404

Parameters used in this example

Parameter Value Description
include candidate Since we're fetching latest job applications, we must include the candidate if we wan't more data about each hire.
filter[stage-type] hired Just list job applications marked as hired
sort -changed_stage_at Sort applications by most recent added to current (hired) stage

Create candidate with a To-Many location relationship

Create a candidates resource with a To-Many relationship to a locations resource set.

The location resource has to be created before this request is executed.

POST https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/candidates HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Token token=abc123abc123
X-Api-Version: 20240404
{"data":{"type":"candidates","attributes":{"email":"jonas@example.com","pitch":"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.","last-name":"Jonas","first-name":"Brusman","merge":true},"relationships":{"locations":{"data":[{"id":"1","type":"locations"}]}}}}

Embed application form

Example iframe

<iframe src="https://career.teamtailor.com/jobs/7199-new-title/applications/new?iframe=true" style="width: 100%; height: 800px" frameborder="0"></iframe>

Iframe helper script

<script src="https://scripts.teamtailor-cdn.com/widgets/production/apply.js"></script>

To embed an application form on your website, create an iframe and set the src attribute to the job's careersite-job-apply-iframe-url attribute. Remember to set frameborder="0" and style="width: 100%; height: 800px". To enable features such as auto-resize of the iframe, insert the helper script to the right in the head section of your page.

Create a job from a template

To create a job from a template you need first to obtain the template ID and then include it in the POST request

POST https://api.teamtailor.com/v1/jobs HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Token token=abc123abc123
Content-Type: application/json
{
    "data":
    {
        "type": "jobs",
        "attributes":
        {
            "title": "Account Manager",
            "pitch": "Become part of something great!",
            "body": "<p class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml'>hello</p>",
            "template-id": 3026014
        },
        "relationships":
        {
            "user":
            {
                "data":
                {
                    "id": 1479857,
                    "type": "users"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

This will copy everything from the template including triggers, application form, etc. Values used in the payload will overwrite the template, so in above example, body will be set to 'Hello'

You can fetch list of templates using GET jobs?filter[status]=template

If you need to fetch a specific template, you can add &filter[template-name]=template_name to the existing filter in the request. For example: GET jobs?filter[status]=template&filter[template-name]=your_template_name

item.description:
Candidates

Required scope: Admin

A candidate is defined by a unqiue email adress. If a candidate don't have any job-applications it can be either sourced or connected.

  • When sourced the candidate was added to the system by a recruiter.

  • When referred the candidate was added to the system by an employee.

  • When connected the candidate has opted in to recieve new job notifications and has also the option to create a richer and more personal profile.

item.description:
Custom field value

A custom field value represents the relationship between custom field and an owner (a candidate or a job).

There are a number of custom field types as specified by the field-type attribute.

  • CustomField::Text any kind of text

  • CustomField::Email valid email address e.g example@example.com

  • CustomField::Url valid url e.g https://google.com

  • CustomField::Phone A phone number, can include any values, eg +46 723 3223 123

  • CustomField::Date Date in ISO 8601 format e.g 2019-08-28

  • CustomField::Checkbox true or false

  • CustomField::Number any number

  • CustomField::Select id for selected CustomFieldOption

  • CustomField::MultiSelect array of ids for selected CustomFieldOption

Attributes

Division availability

Companies using Divisions can restrict a location to some divisions and/or the Main Company. The availability is described by two fields together: the divisions relationship and the available-for-main-company attribute.

divisions available-for-main-company Meaning
[] false Entire Organization: available everywhere (default)
[] true Main Company only
[12] true Division 12 and the Main Company
[12, 34] false Divisions 12 and 34 only

Both fields can be read and written on POST /v1/locations and PATCH /v1/locations/:id. Omitting both on create gives Entire Organization. Sending divisions: [] together with available-for-main-company: false on update clears all restrictions (Entire Organization).

A division id that does not belong to your company returns 404 Not Found.

Warning: narrowing a location's divisions removes that location from every job, employee and approval flow that belongs to a division outside the new list. This is the same behaviour as in the ATS and it cannot be undone by the API.

item.description:
Teams (Groups)

Use teams to customize your users access to the Candidates Pool and to jobs the whole team is considered part of the Hiring Team.

How team rules combine

Granting rules add up (OR): departments, roles, divisions, main-company-all-departments and no-department. A candidate matching any of them is visible to the team's members.

Narrowing rules apply on top (AND): locations. With locations set, the team only reaches candidates in those locations, among the ones the granting rules matched.

all-divisions ("Entire organization") grants every candidate in the company and cannot be combined with any granting rule, the API returns a validation error if you try. It can be combined with narrowing rules: entire organization plus a location means every candidate in that location.

A team with no rules at all grants access to no candidates.

Read more about how to use Teams

true if the team have access to candidates without department.

Default: false.
main-company-all-departments boolean If Divisions Add-on is disabled:
true if the team have access to candidates through all the departments.

If Divisions Add-on is enabled:
true if the team have access to candidates through all the departments in the Main Company.

Default: false.
all_divisions boolean true if the team have access to candidates in the Entire Organization (so through all the departments through all the divisions).

Default: false.

Available only if Divisions Add-on is enabled.

item.name: Transient Uploads

request.description:
Uploads a file to temporary storage and returns a transient URI that can be used in place of a public URL in some endpoints. This is useful if you are not able to provide public URLs for us to retrieve files from.

The transient URI is a unique, tamper-proof token that allows us (and only us) to retrieve the uploaded file from temporary storage and attach it to another resource (like a Candidate). It is exposed only once in the response from this endpoint, so you must take care to store it until you are ready to use it. If you lose the transient URI for an uploaded file, you must upload the file again to get a new URI.

As the name implies, files uploaded to this endpoint are not stored permanently. You are expected to use the URI immediately to attach the uploaded file to another resource.

Note: Unlike other endpoints in our public API, this endpoint accepts form data requests, not JSON. The response is always JSON.

item.description: The Transient Uploads API provides an endpoint for uploading a file to temporary storage for use in subsequent requests.
